acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Sean Cole guest hosts. A mix tape’s not-so-hidden message gets lost to the machine.

acts.label: Track One
acts.desc:
As a kid, Nichole Perkins always liked a very specific type of song. But as an adult, those songs took on a more practical use: a roadmap to navigating love in unexpected places.
This story was based on a chapter of Nichole’s memoir, Sometimes I Trip on How Happy We Could Be.
acts.title: Just Be Good to Me

acts.label: Track Two
acts.desc: Sean Cole plays a minute of a tune he’s had stuck in his head. Happily. It’s a song about unburdening yourself through music.
acts.title: Music is Easy

acts.label: Track Three
acts.desc: Producer Chana Joffe-Walt really loves the slideshows that schools display at end-of-the-year parent assemblies. A lot. But one in particular wasn’t doing it for her.
acts.title: The End of the Road

acts.label: Track Four
acts.desc: A lot of music discovery happens when we are kids. Ken Eglin discovered a lot of music when he was way older, and became low-key famous for what he had to say about it.
acts.title: What’s the Frequency, Kenneth?

acts.label: Track Five
acts.desc: We had a song made just for you.
acts.title: I Talk in Tunes
